title: Consumer legislation and contract terms
summary: Consumer-protection statutes can impose requirements and remedies even when ordinary rules of assent and consideration would recognize a contract.
notes:
Doe applies New York’s dating-services legislation to contracts that attempted to describe the service as something outside the statute. The court examined what the service actually did and the mandatory terms and price rules governing it. The agreement’s own characterization did not determine the statute’s coverage.

The casebook compares judicial review, legislation, administrative enforcement, and European controls on unfair terms. Those approaches may regulate disclosure, substantive terms, or remedies. Keep each source’s coverage and remedy separate; a rule requiring readable disclosure does not necessarily decide whether a clearly disclosed term is substantively fair.
